data.long_meaning: The name Ksenija is of Slavic origin and translates to 'descendant of Xenia'. Xenia was a Greek goddess of hospitality, and the name Ksenija is derived from her name. The name signifies grace and hospitality. The name Ksenija carries the meaning “Grace, descendant of Xenia” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ksenija usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, descendant of xenia and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the grace and hospitality of God, inviting others into our lives and homes.
data.etymology: Ksenija belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grace, descendant of Xenia.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ksenija total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

The name has been popular among Slavic Christians, particularly in the Eastern Orthodox Church, where the manifestation of hospitality and love towards others is a significant aspect of the faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ksenija holds spiritual significance as a reflection of the Christian virtues of love, kindness, and hospitality. It symbolizes the call to carry the spirit of Xenia and extend a welcoming hand to all, just as Jesus did. The name serves as a reminder to honor and practice the principle of hospitality towards others, which is essential to nurturing meaningful relationships and fostering a loving community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ksenija, derived from Xenia in Greek, signifies hospitality and kindness towards strangers and guests. It symbolizes the Christian virtue of extending love and compassion to all, reflecting the spirit of Christ.

historical_references.reference: Ksenija of Lithuania, also known as Alexandra, was the queen consort of King Sigismund I the Old of Poland in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. She was a devout and learned woman who helped promote the Renaissance in Poland. She was known for her patronage of artists, scholars, and the arts.
